arxiv-1804-11071.title: Numerical estimation of wavefront error breakdown in adaptive optics
arxiv-1804-11071.creator: F. Ferreira, E. Gendron, G. Rousset, D. Gratadour
arxiv-1804-11071.description: Abstract Aims. Adaptive optics (AO) system performance is improved using post-processing techniques, such as point spread function (PSF) deconvolution. The PSF estimation involves characterization of the different wavefront (WF) error sources in the AO system. We propose a numerical error breakdown estimation tool that allows studying AO error source behavior such as their correlations.

arxiv-2103-12903.title: Joint Dynamic Models and Statistical Inference for Recurrent Competing Risks, Longitudinal Marker, and Health Status
arxiv-2103-12903.creator: Lili Tong, Piaomu Liu, Edsel A. Peña
arxiv-2103-12903.description: Abstract Consider a subject or unit in a longitudinal biomedical, public health, engineering, economic, or social science study which is being monitored over a possibly random duration. Over time this unit experiences competing recurrent events and a longitudinal marker transitions over a discrete state-space.

arxiv-2207-14717.title: Bayesian nonparametric mixture inconsistency for the number of components: How worried should we be in practice?
arxiv-2207-14717.creator: Yannis Chaumeny yannis.chaumeny@alumni.epfl.chDepartment of StatisticsEcole Polytechnique Fédérale de LausanneLausanne, Switzerland, Johan van der Molen Moris johan.vdmolen@mrc-bsu.cam.ac.ukMRC Biostatistics UnitUniversity of CambridgeCambridge, UKAnthony C. Davison anthony.davison@epfl.chDepartment
arxiv-2207-14717.description: Abstract We consider the Bayesian mixture of finite mixtures (MFMs) and Dirichlet process mixture (DPM) models for clustering. Recent asymptotic theory has established that DPMs overestimate the number of clusters for large samples and that estimators from both classes of models are inconsistent for the number of clusters under misspecification, but the implications for finite sample analyses are unclear.

arxiv-2308-11420.title: Supply Function Equilibrium in Networked Electricity Markets
arxiv-2308-11420.creator: Yuanzhang Xiao, Chaithanya Bandi, and Ermin Wei
arxiv-2308-11420.description: Abstract We study deregulated power markets with strategic power suppliers. In deregulated markets, each supplier submits its supply function (i.e., the amount of electricity it is willing to produce at various prices) to the independent system operator (ISO), who based on the submitted supply functions, dispatches the suppliers to clear the market with minimal total generation cost.

arxiv-2309-01330.title: A thin plate approximation for ocean wave interactions with an ice shelf
arxiv-2309-01330.creator: Luke G. Bennetts, Timothy D. Williams, Richard Porter
arxiv-2309-01330.description: Abstract A variational principle is proposed to derive the governing equations for the problem of ocean wave interactions with a floating ice shelf, where the ice shelf is modelled by the full linear equations of elasticity and has an Archimedean draught.

arxiv-2309-15151.title: Small-scale signatures of primordial non-Gaussianity in k-Nearest Neighbour cumulative distribution functions
arxiv-2309-15151.creator: William R. Coulton, Tom Abel, Arka Banerjee
arxiv-2309-15151.description: Abstract Searches for primordial non-Gaussianity in cosmological perturbations are a key means of revealing novel primordial physics. However, robustly extracting signatures of primordial non-Gaussianity from non-linear scales of the late-time Universe is an open problem. In this paper, we apply k-Nearest Neighbor cumulative distribution functions, kNN-CDFs, to the quijote-png simulations to explore the sensitivity of kNN-CDFs to primordial non-Gaussianity.

arxiv-2405-00402.title: Self-Refine Instruction-Tuning for Aligning Reasoning in Language Models
arxiv-2405-00402.creator: Leonardo Ranaldi, Andrè Freitas ( † ) {(\dagger)} Idiap Research Institute, Martigny, Switzerland ( ∗ ) {(*)} Department of Computer Science, University of Manchester, UK
arxiv-2405-00402.description: Abstract The alignments of reasoning abilities between smaller and larger Language Models are largely conducted via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) using demonstrations generated from robust Large Language Models (LLMs). Although these approaches deliver more performant models, they do not show sufficiently strong generalization ability as the training only relies on the provided demonstrations.

arxiv-2508-20901.title: Lattice path combinatorics in superconformal Yang-Mills theories Unité Mixte de Recherche 3681 du CNRS
arxiv-2508-20901.creator: G.P. Korchemsky
arxiv-2508-20901.description: Abstract We study a class of observables in four-dimensional superconformal Yang–Mills theories which, in the planar limit at finite ’t Hooft coupling, can be expressed as determinants of semi-infinite matrices built from Bessel functions. This determinant representation points to an underlying integrable structure, which we make explicit by showing that the observables satisfy a nonlinear differential-difference equation.

pmc-10526354.title: Ribonucleoside Hydrolases–Structure, Functions, Physiological Role and Practical Uses
pmc-10526354.creator: Leonid A Shaposhnikov, Svyatoslav S Savin, Vladimir I Tishkov, Anastasia A Pometun, Yung-Chuan Liu, Jose M Guisan, Antonio Zuorro
pmc-10526354.description: Ribonucleoside hydrolases are enzymes that catalyze the cleavage of ribonucleosides to nitrogenous bases and ribose. These enzymes are found in many organisms: bacteria, archaea, protozoa, metazoans, yeasts, fungi and plants. Despite the simple reaction catalyzed by these enzymes, their physiological role in most organisms remains unclear.

pmc-10672303.title: Thermal Regeneration of Spent Sand with Furfuryl Binder from an Ecological and Economic Point of View
pmc-10672303.creator: Mariusz Łucarz, Michał Dereń, Rodrigo Moreno
pmc-10672303.description: The recovery of the grain matrix from spent moulding sand is a constant challenge in making the best possible use of the deposits of quartz sand material, as well as in protecting them. In the case of spent sand with organic binders, the best method to recover the grain matrix is thermal regeneration.

pmc-10675584.title: Evaluating the Potential of Plukenetia volubilis Linneo (Sacha Inchi) in Alleviating Cardiovascular Disease Risk Factors: A Mini Review
pmc-10675584.creator: Izzat Zulhilmi Abd Rahman, Nur Syahidah Nor Hisam, Amilia Aminuddin, Adila A Hamid, Jaya Kumar, Azizah Ugusman, Adelina Vlad, Dorin Dragoş
pmc-10675584.description: Plukenetia volubilis Linneo or Sacha Inchi (SI), a traditional natural remedy indigenous to Peru and Brazil, has garnered global attention due to its exceptional nutritional composition. Its protective effects against various non-communicable diseases, notably cardiovascular disease (CVD), have become a subject of interest in recent research.

pmc-10715912.title: Exact calculation of end-of-outbreak probabilities using contact tracing data
pmc-10715912.creator: N. V. Bradbury, W. S. Hart, F. A. Lovell-Read, J. A. Polonsky, R. N. Thompson
pmc-10715912.description: A key challenge for public health policymakers is determining when an infectious disease outbreak has finished. Following a period without cases, an estimate of the probability that no further cases will occur in future (the end-of-outbreak probability) can be used to inform whether or not to declare an outbreak over.

pmc-11498353.title: Trends and Public Perception of Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging: A Social Media Analysis
pmc-11498353.creator: Mansour Almanaa
pmc-11498353.description: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) in medical imaging has generated significant interest and debate among healthcare professionals, researchers, and the general public. This study aims to explore trends and public perception of AI in medical imaging by analyzing social media discussions.

pmc-12438288.title: Thirteen-Year Trajectories of Depressive and Anxiety Symptoms in Individuals with and without Migraine: Insights from the NESDA Cohort
pmc-12438288.creator: N. Van Veelen, N. Pelzer, B. Penninx, G. M. Terwindt, E. J. Giltay
pmc-12438288.description: IntroductionMigraine is strongly associated with depressive and anxiety disorders, as migraine patients have over a twofold higher risk of major depressive disorder and nearly a threefold higher risk of anxiety disorders compared to non-migraine individuals.ObjectivesThis study investigates the 13-year trajectories in individuals with a depression or anxiety disorder with and without comorbid migraine.

pmc-12510894.title: A Preterm Infant With Gestational Age of 21+4 Weeks
pmc-12510894.creator: Haifeng Zong, Bingchun Lin, Yingsui Huang, Shan Jiang, Yurong Yuan, Xiaoyuan Xiong, Zhichun Feng, Chuanzhong Yang
pmc-12510894.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). We report a case of a male infant who was conceived through in vitro fertilization, with a gestational age of 21+4 weeks. The infant was discharged home at 42 weeks' postmenstrual age without significant cranial morbidities.Keywords: extremely low birth weight, extremely preterm, newborn, premature Introduction Periviable gestation, as the gestational age (GA) spectrum, is accompanied by severe morbidity and mortality rates in survivors at the lower threshold.

pmc-13624314.title: Special Interests in Autism: Functions, Benefits, and Challenges
pmc-13624314.creator: Mareike Bayer, Isabel Dziobek
pmc-13624314.description: Special interests are a highly prevalent feature of autism spectrum conditions (ASC) and have long been described primarily from a deficit-oriented perspective. More recent work has pointed to their potential as psychological resources, yet systematic evidence and direct comparisons with non-autistic groups remain limited.
